prompt_text: Where should I stay in Branson Missouri, an Airbnb or a hotel, and which specific places are best?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: it depends on what you want to do. If you want convenience for shows, restaurants and nightlife, a hotel on or near 76/Branson Landing is usually best. If you want quiet, outdoor time, boating or a multi-family/group stay, an Airbnb (lakefront cabin or whole-home rental) is often better. Below are quick pros/cons, where to stay by activity, recommended hotels, and how to pick an Airbnb.

Pros/cons (quick)
- Hotel: predictable service, daily housekeeping, on‑site front desk, pools, breakfast and concierge/ticket help, good for short stays and show/Strip proximity. Easier for mobility needs.
- Airbnb/cabin: more space, kitchen, lower per-person cost for groups, private outdoor space (decks/hot tubs/lake docks), feels like “getting away.” More variable quality, check-in can be self-service, cleaning/extra fees vary.

Where to stay by priority
- Seeing shows & nightlife (76 Country Blvd / Branson Strip or Branson Landing): stay on/near the Strip or Branson Landing for walking access to theaters, restaurants, shops.
- Family with kids / short visit: hotels on the Strip or with pools and breakfast are easiest.
- Silver Dollar City & the Ozarks (rides + fall foliage): stay in/near Branson West, Indian Point, or the Silver Dollar City area to cut drive time.
- Lake/boating/relaxation: Table Rock Lake, Indian Point, Hollister, Kimberling City, or properties on Taneycomo for trout fishing — choose lakefront cabins or resorts.
- Large groups/extended stays: whole cabins or multi-bedroom condos (Airbnb/VRBO) or suite-style hotels.

Recommended hotels (by category)
- Luxury / lakefront & spa: Chateau on the Lake Resort, Spa & Convention Center — upscale, lake views, spa, good for romantic getaways.
- Resort + outdoors closeby: Big Cedar Lodge (a short drive north of Branson) — excellent if you want a resort, golf, marina and cabins.
- Convenient to shows & shopping: Hilton Branson Convention Center — central to Branson Landing and the Strip.
- Branson Landing / shops & lakefront dining: Radisson Hotel Branson (on/near Branson Landing) or similar Landing-area hotels — easy walking to restaurants and the crepe/boardwalk area.
- Boutique / unique: The Keeter Center at College of the Ozarks (small, distinctive, good food) — quieter, well‑kept.
- Budget / family chains (good value): Holiday Inn Express, Best Western, Comfort Inn along 76 — practical, pool and breakfast.

What to look for in an Airbnb in Branson
- Location: “Table Rock Lake,” “Indian Point,” “Hollister,” or “Branson West” for lake/cabin stays. “Branson Landing” or “76 Country Blvd” for proximity to shows.
- Type: whole cabin/house for privacy, hot tub and game room for groups, lakefront with dock if boating.
- Filters: Superhost, 4.8+ rating, review count (more reviews = more reliable), clear cancellation and cleaning fees.
- Amenities: parking, AC, strong Wi‑Fi if you need streaming, outdoor grill, hot tub, washer/dryer, no-stairs options if accessibility matters.

Money & booking tips
- Compare total cost (nightly + cleaning + service + taxes) vs hotel room + resort fee. For groups, per-person cost often favors a rental.
- Book early for peak times (summer, school breaks, fall festival weekends).
- For shows, consider a hotel for late-night return and for help with tickets/transport.
- Read recent reviews closely for cleanliness, accuracy of listing, and host responsiveness.

If you tell me: dates, how many people, budget range, and whether you want shows or lake time, I can:
- suggest 2–3 specific hotels that will be available for those dates, and/or
- look for 3–5 Airbnb/VRBO-style listings that match your needs and sleep count.

Which would you prefer me to do — suggest hotels or search Airbnb-style rentals for your dates and party size?
